overall_summary: Crypto faces a clearly risk-off day as record Bitcoin ETF outflows, heavy stablecoin redemptions, and rising liquidations pressure price. A strong dollar, sticky inflation talk, and fresh tariff threats add macro headwinds, while geopolitics stays messy. The lone bright spot is CFTC reserve treatment for BTC and ETH, but it is outweighed by the selling and caution.
key_points: CFTC allows BTC/ETH as exchange reserves
Dollar and yields firm; inflation still elevated
Tariff threats and geopolitics raise risk premium

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Hit Record $4.7B+ November Outflows
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted another day of heavy net outflows around two hundred thirty million dollars on the twenty-fourth, extending a six-day streak and pushing November totals past four point seven billion dollars to a new monthly record. BlackRock's IBIT led the redemptions again. Bitcoin slipped back under sixty thousand dollars and traded near fifty-nine thousand as the selling pressure continued. Traders should care because sustained institutional outflows remove a key source of demand and keep downside pressure alive ahead of key data.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker institutional bid

items.title: CFTC Lets BTC and ETH Count Toward Exchange Reserves
items.summary: CFTC staff issued an advisory allowing bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins to count toward the twelve-month operating expense reserves that derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses must hold, subject to haircuts of at least twenty percent for bitcoin and ether. Crypto still cannot meet the separate liquidity requirement. This is a meaningful regulatory nod that reduces capital friction for regulated venues. Traders should watch it as a longer-term positive for institutional infrastructure and potential balance-sheet demand.
items.impact: Eases capital rules for crypto derivatives platforms

items.title: Stablecoin Redemptions Hit Twelve Billion in Thirty Days
items.summary: Net redemptions across major stablecoins reached about twelve billion dollars over thirty days through mid-November, according to Kaiko, with USDT and USDC each shrinking roughly four percent. Analysts say the pattern looks more like capital exiting crypto entirely rather than rotating inside the market, echoing the two thousand twenty-two bear period though on a smaller scale. Supply contraction has slowed recently. This matters because fewer stablecoins on exchanges and wallets mean less dry powder available to buy dips.
items.impact: Reduced on-exchange liquidity and buying power

items.title: DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion USDC from Binance Hack
items.summary: The US Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking more than one point one billion dollars in USDC tied to the October Binance hack attributed to North Korean actors. Circle has frozen the tokens and agreed to issue replacement USDC to the government if the court grants forfeiture. Authorities say they have helped freeze, seize or return over two point nine billion overall from the roughly six billion stolen. This is a major recovery step but also keeps the largest crypto theft and associated risks in the headlines.
items.impact: Highlights recovery progress and lingering hack risks

items.title: Ark Invest Sells $6.8 Million of Its Own Bitcoin ETF
items.summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest sold roughly six point eight million dollars worth of shares in its own Ark twenty-one Shares Bitcoin ETF on Tuesday through one of its other funds as bitcoin dipped below fifty-nine thousand. The firm also trimmed other crypto-linked holdings. This comes amid the broader ETF outflow wave. Traders notice when a high-profile manager reduces exposure to its own product during a weak tape, adding to the sense of institutional caution.

items.title: Bitcoin Reverses Nvidia Spike as Liquidations Climb
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly spiked toward sixty-five thousand on the Nvidia CEO news then fully reversed, falling back under sixty thousand with hundreds of millions in futures liquidations over twenty-four hours, mostly longs. The move highlighted how equity-driven pumps are fading quickly in crypto while ETF outflows and macro caution dominate. Fear readings remain extreme. Short-term traders should treat these failed rallies as confirmation of weak underlying demand until flows stabilize.
items.impact: Failed bounce reinforces downside bias near-term

items.title: Core PCE, GDP revision due today ahead of Dec Fed
items.summary: October Core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, hits at 8:30 AM Eastern along with the Q3 GDP second estimate, personal income and spending, durable goods, and jobless claims. Core is expected around 0.3 percent month-over-month and 3.2 percent year-over-year, up from 3.1 percent, while GDP is seen near the 3.4 percent advance. This is the last major inflation print before the December FOMC, where markets price roughly 95 to 98 percent odds of a 25 basis point hike. Traders should care because a hot print locks in tighter policy and stronger dollar pressure on risk assets including Bitcoin, while a cool one could ease some of the hawkish positioning in a holiday-shortened week.
items.impact: High volatility catalyst for rates, DXY, and crypto risk appetite

items.title: Consumer confidence surges to 103.3, highest since early 2025
items.summary: The Conference Board index jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, crushing forecasts near 92 and reaching the highest level since January 2025. Present situation and expectations both rose sharply, driven by much stronger views of the job market with more consumers saying jobs are plentiful. Inflation expectations eased a bit but stayed elevated. This is somewhat hawkish for the Fed as it points to resilient demand heading into the holidays, supporting the case for further rate hikes if PCE also stays sticky.
items.impact: Supports higher-for-longer rates and firmer USD, pressuring risk assets

items.title: Trump admin readies new Section 301 tariffs on China, EU, others
items.summary: The administration is set to unveil findings from a Section 301 probe into excess industrial capacity and subsidies covering China, the EU, and about 14 other economies, with new tariffs expected soon. Rates are likely to stay within existing deal caps such as 15 percent for the EU, Japan and South Korea and the 20 percent ceiling on China under the current truce, targeting mostly manufactured goods while carving out autos, steel and some others. Markets are already reacting with risk-off flows. Crypto traders should watch this because fresh tariffs can stoke inflation fears, lift the dollar, and hit global growth and risk sentiment.
items.impact: Potential inflation impulse and risk-off for equities and crypto

items.title: Williams says inflation still too high, more hikes needed over time
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said Monday that inflation remains too high and the Fed still has work to do to get it back to 2 percent on a sustained basis. He tied future actions to incoming data ahead of the December meeting and indicated policy will need to tighten further over time. Markets already heavily price a December hike from the current 3.75-4.00 percent range. This reinforces the hawkish backdrop for today's PCE print and keeps rate-cut hopes pushed out, which typically weighs on Bitcoin via higher real yields and a stronger dollar.
items.impact: Solidifies December hike odds and higher-for-longer narrative

items.title: Dollar firms near multi-month highs as yields stay elevated
items.summary: The DXY is holding firm around 104 or recently testing higher levels, supported by sticky inflation expectations and near-certain December Fed hike pricing. Ten-year Treasury yields have been trading near 4.87 to 4.91 percent after recent peaks, with some dip ahead of the data but still elevated. Risk-off from tech and tariff talk is also lifting the greenback. For crypto this matters because a strong dollar and high real yields usually act as a headwind for Bitcoin and other risk assets in the short run.
items.impact: USD strength and higher yields pressure crypto and equities

items.title: Fed Beige Book due this afternoon before Thanksgiving
items.summary: The Federal Reserve releases its latest Beige Book at 2 PM Eastern, summarizing anecdotal conditions across the twelve districts. It comes two weeks before the December FOMC and after recent data showing solid but uneven growth with persistent price pressures. Previous editions pointed to modest expansion led by manufacturing and AI-related investment alongside consumer caution. Traders will parse language on inflation stickiness, labor tightness, and demand for any shift in the policy outlook right before the holiday close.
items.impact: Secondary read on economy that can nudge rate-path expectations

items.title: Houthi Drones Hit Riyadh Financial Tower Again
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis struck a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District with a drone, injuring eleven people including Saudis and foreign workers. It is the second hit on the same landmark housing the Public Investment Fund in under a week, and the group also claimed attacks toward Ras Tanura refinery while threatening Saudi Red Sea ports. This spills over from the wider US-Iran conflict and raises fresh risks to Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping. Traders should watch oil premiums and risk-off moves if the Saudi-led coalition responds forcefully.
items.impact: Higher oil volatility and geo risk premium pressure risk assets

items.title: US Readies New Tariffs on China, EU and Others
items.summary: The Trump administration is set to announce fresh import tariffs on China, the European Union, India, Japan and about a dozen other partners after a probe into excess industrial capacity. Rates are expected to vary by country and partly replace earlier duties struck down by the Supreme Court, while still respecting some existing caps. This reopens trade tensions just weeks after midterms and a China meeting. Crypto traders care because broader tariffs hit global growth expectations and can spark risk-off selling across equities and digital assets.
items.impact: Growth fears and trade uncertainty weigh on risk appetite

items.title: Ukrainian Drones Set Russian Oil Refineries Ablaze
items.summary: Overnight Ukrainian drone strikes hit Rosneft's Syzran and Kuibyshev refineries in Russia's Samara region, sparking large fires according to local reports and OSINT. The regional governor said more than 145 drones were downed, one person killed and power outages followed, while Putin called retaliation inevitable. These attacks continue a campaign that has already damaged a large share of Russian refining capacity. Energy markets and risk assets react because tighter product supplies can lift oil and diesel prices and keep geopolitical risk elevated.
items.impact: Oil supply disruption risk and escalation fears hit sentiment

items.title: Huawei Convicted on US Sanctions and Trade-Secret Charges
items.summary: A Brooklyn federal jury found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty on ten of twelve counts including bank fraud, wire fraud, Iran sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. It was acquitted of racketeering and obstruction. Sentencing is set for September 2027 with potentially large fines, and Huawei plans to appeal. The verdict hardens US-China tech decoupling just as new tariffs loom. Markets watch it as another signal of sustained friction that can pressure global tech supply chains and risk assets.
items.impact: US-China tech tensions add to risk-off pressure

items.title: Ukraine Expands War by Sinking Russian Ship in Libya
items.summary: Ukraine confirmed it used naval drones to sink the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi naval base and strike a cargo vessel used for weapons transport. Two Libyan soldiers were reported killed and the operation extends the Russia-Ukraine conflict into the Mediterranean and oil-rich North Africa. Eastern Libyan authorities and the Tripoli government both condemned the spillover. Traders note the geographic widening raises odds of broader instability and secondary sanctions or energy route disruptions.
items.impact: War widening increases global instability premium

items.title: Trump Weighs Targeting Iranian Leaders Amid Hormuz Tensions
items.summary: NBC and other reports say the Trump administration is discussing options that include targeted strikes on senior Iranian leaders as the window for larger military action narrows with funding running into January. Iran's IRGC claimed oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz while new US sanctions hit Iranian shadow banking networks, sending the rial lower. Diplomacy remains stalled in a no-war-no-peace standoff. Crypto and risk markets care because any sharp escalation or Hormuz disruption would spike oil and trigger classic risk-off flows.
items.impact: Unresolved escalation risk keeps oil and volatility elevated
